jewellery.summary: Worn, broken, inherited or unwanted — in any condition.
jewellery.body: Chains, rings, bracelets, earrings and pendants, whether whole or in pieces. Nothing needs to be a matching pair, in working order, or worth anything in particular before it is worth bringing in.
jewellery.imageAlt: A wide diamond-set gold bangle photographed against black, its stones catching a single warm light.

silver.summary: Sterling, coin silver, and other solid-silver items.
silver.body: We buy solid silver, including sterling marked 925, jewelry, flatware, serving pieces, coin silver, and many foreign grades such as 800 or 835 silver. Silver-plated items are not purchased.
silver.imageAlt: A silver filigree butterfly pendant among fine chains and carved shell blossoms, on black.

coins.summary: U.S. and world precious-metal coins, whether collected or inherited.
coins.body: Coins are assessed for their precious-metal content while also considering whether an obvious collectible premium may exceed melt value. If we believe a coin may be worth more as a collectible than for its metal alone, we will tell you.
coins.imageAlt: A hammered gold sovereign, its shield-and-Tudor-rose reverse struck in deep relief, lit against a dark ground.

bullion.summary: Investment bars and coins, assessed on weight and stated fineness.
bullion.body: Refiner marks and stated fineness are checked against the physical weight of the piece. Recognized bullion is handled on its own terms rather than treated as scrap metal.
bullion.imageAlt: Three cast gold bars stacked on a dark surface under a shaft of warm light, scattered with small gold grains, carrying no refiner markings.
